verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.51
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 7.51

verses.pali: 5. Mahāyaññavagga
verses.english: 5. A Great Sacrifice

verses.pali: Saṁyogasutta
verses.english: Yoking and Unyoking

verses.pali: “Saṁyogavisaṁyogaṁ vo, bhikkhave, dhammapariyāyaṁ desessāmi.
verses.english: “Mendicants, I will teach you an exposition of the teaching on yoking and unyoking.

verses.pali: Taṁ suṇātha …pe…
verses.english: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak. …

verses.pali: katamo ca so, bhikkhave, saṁyogo visaṁyogo dhammapariyāyo?
verses.english: And what is the exposition of the teaching on yoking and unyoking?

verses.pali: Itthī, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṁ itthindriyaṁ manasi karoti—
verses.english: A woman focuses on her own femininity:

verses.pali: itthikuttaṁ itthākappaṁ itthividhaṁ itthicchandaṁ itthissaraṁ itthālaṅkāraṁ.
verses.english: her feminine moves, feminine appearance, feminine ways, feminine desires, feminine voice, and feminine adornment.

verses.pali: Sā tattha rajjati tatrābhiramati.
verses.english: She’s stimulated by this and takes pleasure in it.

verses.pali: Sā tattha rattā tatrābhiratā bahiddhā purisindriyaṁ manasi karoti—
verses.english: So she focuses on the masculinity of others:

verses.pali: purisakuttaṁ purisākappaṁ purisavidhaṁ purisacchandaṁ purisassaraṁ purisālaṅkāraṁ.
verses.english: masculine moves, masculine appearance, masculine ways, masculine desires, masculine voice, and masculine adornment.

verses.pali: Sā tattha rajjati tatrābhiramati.
verses.english: She’s stimulated by this and takes pleasure in it.

verses.pali: Sā tattha rattā tatrābhiratā bahiddhā saṁyogaṁ ākaṅkhati.
verses.english: So she desires to yoke herself to another.

verses.pali: Yañcassā saṁyogapaccayā uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ tañca ākaṅkhati.
verses.english: And she desires the pleasure and happiness that comes from such yoking.

verses.pali: Itthatte, bhikkhave, abhiratā sattā purisesu saṁyogaṁ gatā.
verses.english: Sentient beings who relish their femininity are yoked to men.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, itthī itthattaṁ nātivattati.
verses.english: This is how a woman does not transcend her femininity.

verses.pali: Puriso, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṁ purisindriyaṁ manasi karoti—
verses.english: A man focuses on his own masculinity:

verses.pali: purisakuttaṁ purisākappaṁ purisavidhaṁ purisacchandaṁ purisassaraṁ purisālaṅkāraṁ.
verses.english: his masculine moves, masculine appearance, masculine ways, masculine desires, masculine voice, and masculine adornment.

verses.pali: So tattha rajjati tatrābhiramati.
verses.english: He’s stimulated by this and takes pleasure in it.

verses.pali: So tattha ratto tatrābhirato bahiddhā itthindriyaṁ manasi karoti—
verses.english: So he focuses on the femininity of others:

verses.pali: itthikuttaṁ itthākappaṁ itthividhaṁ itthicchandaṁ itthissaraṁ itthālaṅkāraṁ.
verses.english: feminine moves, feminine appearance, feminine ways, feminine desires, feminine voice, and feminine adornment.

verses.pali: So tattha rajjati tatrābhiramati.
verses.english: He’s stimulated by this and takes pleasure in it.

verses.pali: So tattha ratto tatrābhirato bahiddhā saṁyogaṁ ākaṅkhati.
verses.english: So he desires to yoke himself to another.

verses.pali: Yañcassa saṁyogapaccayā uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ tañca ākaṅkhati.
verses.english: And he desires the pleasure and happiness that comes from such yoking.

verses.pali: Purisatte, bhikkhave, abhiratā sattā itthīsu saṁyogaṁ gatā.
verses.english: Sentient beings who relish their masculinity are yoked to women.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puriso purisattaṁ nātivattati.
verses.english: This is how a man does not transcend his masculinity.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, saṁyogo hoti.
verses.english: This is how yoking comes about.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, visaṁyogo hoti?
verses.english: And how does unyoking come about?

verses.pali: Itthī, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṁ itthindriyaṁ na manasi karoti—
verses.english: A woman doesn’t focus on her own femininity:

verses.pali: itthikuttaṁ itthākappaṁ itthividhaṁ itthicchandaṁ itthissaraṁ itthālaṅkāraṁ.
verses.english: her feminine moves, feminine appearance, feminine ways, feminine desires, feminine voice, and feminine adornment.

verses.pali: Sā tattha na rajjati, sā tatra nābhiramati.
verses.english: She isn’t stimulated by this and takes no pleasure in it.

verses.pali: Sā tattha arattā tatra anabhiratā bahiddhā purisindriyaṁ na manasi karoti—
verses.english: So she doesn’t focus on the masculinity of others:

verses.pali: purisakuttaṁ purisākappaṁ purisavidhaṁ purisacchandaṁ purisassaraṁ purisālaṅkāraṁ.
verses.english: masculine moves, masculine appearance, masculine ways, masculine desires, masculine voice, and masculine adornment.

verses.pali: Sā tattha na rajjati, tatra nābhiramati.
verses.english: She isn’t stimulated by this and takes no pleasure in it.

verses.pali: Sā tattha arattā tatra anabhiratā bahiddhā saṁyogaṁ nākaṅkhati.
verses.english: So she doesn’t desire to yoke herself to another.

verses.pali: Yañcassā saṁyogapaccayā uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ tañca nākaṅkhati.
verses.english: Nor does she desire the pleasure and happiness that comes from such yoking.

verses.pali: Itthatte, bhikkhave, anabhiratā sattā purisesu visaṁyogaṁ gatā.
verses.english: Sentient beings who do not relish their femininity are not yoked to men.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, itthī itthattaṁ ativattati.
verses.english: This is how a woman transcends her femininity.

verses.pali: Puriso, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṁ purisindriyaṁ na manasi karoti—
verses.english: A man doesn’t focus on his own masculinity:

verses.pali: purisakuttaṁ purisākappaṁ purisavidhaṁ purisacchandaṁ purisassaraṁ purisālaṅkāraṁ.
verses.english: masculine moves, masculine appearance, masculine ways, masculine desires, masculine voice, and masculine adornment.

verses.pali: So tattha na rajjati, so tatra nābhiramati.
verses.english: He isn’t stimulated by this and takes no pleasure in it.

verses.pali: So tattha aratto tatra anabhirato bahiddhā itthindriyaṁ na manasi karoti—
verses.english: So he doesn’t focus on the femininity of others:

verses.pali: itthikuttaṁ itthākappaṁ itthividhaṁ itthicchandaṁ itthissaraṁ itthālaṅkāraṁ.
verses.english: feminine moves, feminine appearance, feminine ways, feminine desires, feminine voice, and feminine adornment.

verses.pali: So tattha na rajjati, tatra nābhiramati.
verses.english: He isn’t stimulated by this and takes no pleasure in it.

verses.pali: So tattha aratto tatra anabhirato bahiddhā saṁyogaṁ nākaṅkhati.
verses.english: So he doesn’t desire to yoke himself to another.

verses.pali: Yañcassa saṁyogapaccayā uppajjati sukhaṁ somanassaṁ tañca nākaṅkhati.
verses.english: Nor does he desire the pleasure and happiness that comes from such yoking.

verses.pali: Purisatte, bhikkhave, anabhiratā sattā itthīsu visaṁyogaṁ gatā.
verses.english: Sentient beings who do not relish their masculinity are not yoked to women.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puriso purisattaṁ ativattati.
verses.english: This is how a man transcends his masculinity.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, visaṁyogo hoti.
verses.english: This is how unyoking comes about.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, saṁyogo visaṁyogo dhammapariyāyo”ti.
verses.english: This is the exposition of the teaching on yoking and unyoking.”

verses.pali: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
